<bpmn:definitions xmlns:bpmn="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL" id="Definitions_SupplierOnboarding" targetNamespace="http://example.com/bpmn/supplier-onboarding">
  <bpmn:message id="Message_RFP" name="Request for proposal"/>
  <bpmn:message id="Message_Proposal" name="Supplier proposal received"/>
  <bpmn:collaboration id="Collaboration_SupplierOnboarding">
    <bpmn:participant id="Participant_Company" name="Company / Procurement team" processRef="Process_SupplierOnboarding"/>
    <bpmn:participant id="Participant_Suppliers" name="Suppliers"/>
    <bpmn:messageFlow id="MessageFlow_RFP" name="Send RFP" sourceRef="Task_IssueRFP" targetRef="Participant_Suppliers"/>
    <bpmn:messageFlow id="MessageFlow_Proposal" name="Proposal response" sourceRef="Participant_Suppliers" targetRef="Event_ProposalsReceived"/>
  </bpmn:collaboration>
  <bpmn:process id="Process_SupplierOnboarding" name="Supplier selection and onboarding" isExecutable="false">
    <bpmn:startEvent id="Event_NeedIdentified" name="Need for new supplier identified"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_IssueRFP" name="Issue request for proposals (RFP)"/>
    <bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent id="Event_ProposalsReceived" name="Proposals received from suppliers">
      <bpmn:messageEventDefinition id="MessageEventDefinition_Proposals" messageRef="Message_Proposal"/>
    </bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_EvaluateProposals" name="Evaluate proposals (cost, quality, delivery time)"/>
    <bpmn:exclusiveGateway id="Gateway_VisitSplit" name="Site visits or interviews needed?" default="Flow_VisitSkipped"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_VisitsInterviews" name="Conduct site visits or interviews with suppliers"/>
    <bpmn:exclusiveGateway id="Gateway_VisitJoin" name="Visit step completed"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_SelectSupplier" name="Analyze and select supplier"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_NegotiateContract" name="Negotiate contract terms"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_SignContract" name="Sign contract"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_OnboardSupplier" name="Onboard supplier and execute contract"/>
    <bpmn:endEvent id="Event_ProcessEnd" name="Supplier onboarded and contract executed"/>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_1" sourceRef="Event_NeedIdentified" targetRef="Task_IssueRFP"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_2" sourceRef="Task_IssueRFP" targetRef="Event_ProposalsReceived"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_3" sourceRef="Event_ProposalsReceived" targetRef="Task_EvaluateProposals"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_4" sourceRef="Task_EvaluateProposals" targetRef="Gateway_VisitSplit"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_VisitNeeded" name="Yes" sourceRef="Gateway_VisitSplit" targetRef="Task_VisitsInterviews"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_VisitSkipped" name="No" sourceRef="Gateway_VisitSplit" targetRef="Gateway_VisitJoin"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_5" sourceRef="Task_VisitsInterviews" targetRef="Gateway_VisitJoin"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_6" sourceRef="Gateway_VisitJoin" targetRef="Task_SelectSupplier"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_7" sourceRef="Task_SelectSupplier" targetRef="Task_NegotiateContract"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_8" sourceRef="Task_NegotiateContract" targetRef="Task_SignContract"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_9" sourceRef="Task_SignContract" targetRef="Task_OnboardSupplier"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_10" sourceRef="Task_OnboardSupplier" targetRef="Event_ProcessEnd"/>
  </bpmn:process>
</bpmn:definitions>

rules.instruction: When the description says a team sends a request to outside actors and then takes in their returned items as work the team carries out, and no stated occurrence is one the process must wait for before it can continue: Model the taking-in of the returned items as a task placed on the sequence flow after the request task and before the next step that uses them. Do not model it as an intermediate catch event. Reserve an intermediate catch event for an occurrence the process must wait for before it can continue.
rules.situation: the description says a team sends a request to outside actors and then takes in their returned items as work the team carries out, and no stated occurrence is one the process must wait for before it can continue

rules.instruction: When the description states that a participant performs an action (for example, identifying a need) that begins the process, and the action is described as work the participant does rather than as an occurrence that starts the process: Model a generic start event with no label that describes the action. Place a task, named after the participant's action, immediately after that start event and before the first step that follows from it. Do not use the start event label to carry the action.
rules.situation: the description says the process begins when a participant performs an action, such as identifying a need or a requirement, and that action is work the participant carries out rather than an occurrence that starts the process

rules.instruction: When the description offers two alternative ways of performing the same signalling or checking step, joined by 'or', and both alternatives lead to the same next step: Model each alternative as its own task. Place an exclusive gateway before the alternatives, with one labelled outgoing flow per alternative, so that the choice of method is explicit. Join the alternatives with an exclusive merge gateway before the shared next step. Do not collapse the alternatives into one generic task, and do not leave either alternative without its choice gateway.
rules.situation: the description states that an optional step may be carried out in one of several alternative forms joined by 'or' (for example, 'may also do X or Y'), and the process continues after that step

rules.instruction: When the description states that an activity may or may not take place (for example, 'may take place' or 'may occur'), so the activity is optional and its execution depends on circumstances the description leaves open: Model an exclusive gateway before the optional activity, with one outgoing flow into the activity and one skip flow that bypasses it. Place a second exclusive gateway after the activity that merges the activity path and the skip path before the next step. Do not model the optional activity as unconditional in the main sequence.
rules.situation: the description states that an optional activity (for example a visit or an interview) may or may not be performed before a later step, and the activity's own gateways and the skip path have to rejoin the main sequence

rules.instruction: When the description's sentence that states the outcome or end of the process joins two distinct actions with 'and', where one action changes the status of a participant and the other is the performance of a separate commitment: Model each action joined by 'and' as its own task, in the order the sentence gives, and place these tasks in sequence before the end event. Do not merge the joined actions into one task whose label names both, and do not let the end event label carry one of the actions; the end event should only name the outcome reached.
rules.situation: the description's sentence that states the outcome or end of the process joins two distinct actions with 'and', where one action changes the status of a participant and the other is the performance of a separate commitment
